  end

- [Frameworks.GreenLight.PermissionMap](Frameworks.GreenLight.PermissionMap.md): The permission map holds a mapping of permissions to roles. The permission map
is intended to be an implementation detail of the authorization framework.
Convenience functions to build it are provided in other modules.

- [Frameworks.GreenLight.Permissions](Frameworks.GreenLight.Permissions.md): The permissions module provides several functions that create permission
strings and `GreenLight.PermissionMap`s.

- [Frameworks.GreenLight.Plug](Frameworks.GreenLight.Plug.md): This Plug validates the permissions before the request is allowed to proceed.

- [Frameworks.GreenLight.Principal](Frameworks.GreenLight.Principal.md): The principal is used as a representation for any person / thing that can
interact with the system.
- [Frameworks.GreenLight.Public](Frameworks.GreenLight.Public.md): Defines an authorization module.

the menu faces renders Prism's button (`Frameworks.Pixel.button/1`) as a
`<div>`, since the action is the clickable element.

- [Mica](Mica.md): Mica keeps the contexts that define your domain
and business logic.

- [Mica.Authentication.Subject](Mica.Authentication.Subject.md): Subject is a representation of a subject that can be authenticated.

- [Mica.Authorization](Mica.Authorization.md): The authorization system for Mica.

additional roles. They can be nested to create a tree structure.

- [Mica.Factories](Mica.Factories.md): This module provides factory function to be used for tests.

- [Mica.FeatureFlags](Mica.FeatureFlags.md): Feature flags. Systems declare the flags they read (`c:Mica.System.feature_flags/0`),
the SaaS sets their defaults (`c:Mica.SaaS.feature_flags/0`), and the app config
(`config :mica, :features`, and `ENABLED_APP_FEATURES` at runtime) has the final say.

- [Mica.ObanConfig](Mica.ObanConfig.md): Builds the Oban config that `Mica.Application` starts, from `config :mica, Oban`,
the queues and crons the systems declare (`c:Mica.System.oban_queues/0`,
`c:Mica.System.oban_crons/0`) and the plugin names `config :mica, :oban_plugins`

- [Mica.RuntimeConfig](Mica.RuntimeConfig.md): Building blocks for a SaaS's `config/runtime.exs`.
- [Mica.RuntimeConfig.Check](Mica.RuntimeConfig.Check.md): Checks the runtime config of a release before it is started, without starting
the app or connecting to the database
- [Mica.RuntimeConfig.Snapshot](Mica.RuntimeConfig.Snapshot.md): Evaluates a runtime config file against a fixed set of environment variables
and renders the result as stable text, so a change in what an environment
gets shows up as a diff.

- [Mica.Seeds.Test](Mica.Seeds.Test.md): Seeds for the test servers (Fly, multiple testN environments).

- [MicaWeb.Cldr](MicaWeb.Cldr.md): Provides the core functions to retrieve and manage
the CLDR data that supports formatting and localisation.
- [MicaWeb.Cldr.AcceptLanguage](MicaWeb.Cldr.AcceptLanguage.md): Parses HTTP `Accept-Language` header values as defined in
[rfc2616](https://www.w3.org/Protocols/rfc2616/rfc2616-sec14.html#sec14.4).
- [MicaWeb.Cldr.Currency](MicaWeb.Cldr.Currency.md)
- [MicaWeb.Cldr.Date](MicaWeb.Cldr.Date.md)
- [MicaWeb.Cldr.Date.Interval](MicaWeb.Cldr.Date.Interval.md): Interval formats allow for software to format intervals like "Jan 10-12, 2008" as a
shorter and more natural format than "Jan 10, 2008 - Jan 12, 2008". They are designed
to take a start and end date, time or datetime plus a formatting pattern
and use that information to produce a localized format.
- [MicaWeb.Cldr.DateTime](MicaWeb.Cldr.DateTime.md)
- [MicaWeb.Cldr.DateTime.Format](MicaWeb.Cldr.DateTime.Format.md): Manages the Date, TIme and DateTime formats
defined by CLDR.
- [MicaWeb.Cldr.DateTime.Formatter](MicaWeb.Cldr.DateTime.Formatter.md): Implements the compilation and execution of
date, time and datetime formats.
- [MicaWeb.Cldr.DateTime.Interval](MicaWeb.Cldr.DateTime.Interval.md): Interval formats allow for software to format intervals like "Jan 10-12, 2008" as a
shorter and more natural format than "Jan 10, 2008 - Jan 12, 2008". They are designed
to take a start and end date, time or datetime plus a formatting pattern
and use that information to produce a localized format.

to take a start and end date, time or datetime plus a formatting pattern

- [MicaWeb.Cldr.Locale](MicaWeb.Cldr.Locale.md): Backend module that provides functions

- [MicaWeb.Cldr.Number](MicaWeb.Cldr.Number.md): Formats numbers and currencies based upon CLDR's decimal formats specification.

- [Next.Systems.Account.NativeApp](Next.Systems.Account.NativeApp.md): Recognises requests from the Next native apps by their
`NextApp/<version> iOS|Android` user-agent suffix.

- [Next.Systems.Account.NativeHandoff](Next.Systems.Account.NativeHandoff.md): Hands a sign-in through an identity provider back to the Next native apps.
- [Next.Systems.Account.NativeProviderController](Next.Systems.Account.NativeProviderController.md): The pages the Next native apps open in the system sign-in sheet to sign in
through an identity provider; see `Next.Systems.Account.NativeHandoff`.

- [Next.Systems.Account.NativeSigninController](Next.Systems.Account.NativeSigninController.md): JSON calls behind the native Sign-in screen of the Next apps: identify
(send a sign-in code to an email, or point to its identity provider), then
verify the code; or redeem the token of an identity-provider sign-in (see
`Next.Systems.Account.NativeHandoff`). They follow the participant
path of the LiveView flow (`AuthIdentifyPage`, `AuthCodeVerifyPage`, the
redeem step) and share its steps through `Next.Systems.Account.OtpSignin`.
- [Next.Systems.Account.NativeSigninGuard](Next.Systems.Account.NativeSigninGuard.md): Admits only same-origin JSON requests from the Next native apps to the
native sign-in calls.
- [Next.Systems.Account.OtpSignin](Next.Systems.Account.OtpSignin.md): Steps of the email-first OTP sign-in shared by the LiveView pages
(`AuthIdentifyPage`, `AuthCodeVerifyPage` and the redeem step in
`SessionController`) and the native app's JSON calls
(`NativeSigninController`), so both follow the same rules.

- [Next.Systems.Annotation.Pattern](Next.Systems.Annotation.Pattern.md): A protocol for creating Annotation Patterns.
Naming convention:
- Each pattern is named after the type of annotation it creates.
- Each pattern name is a noun, like "Definition", "Parameter", "Retraction", etc.

- [Next.Systems.Annotation.Pattern.Connection](Next.Systems.Annotation.Pattern.Connection.md): A pattern for creating a Connection Annotation.
A Connection is way to express that two annotations are related.

- [Next.Systems.Announcement.AdminPanel](Next.Systems.Announcement.AdminPanel.md): The Announcements tab on the Admin page, for system admins only.
- [Next.Systems.Announcement.AdminView](Next.Systems.Announcement.AdminView.md): The Announcements tab on the Admin page: the list of announcements. A row
opens its announcement, and New announcement a new one, on the page to
compose it (`Next.Systems.Announcement.ComposePage`).
- [Next.Systems.Announcement.AdminViewBuilder](Next.Systems.Announcement.AdminViewBuilder.md): View model of the Announcements tab: every announcement, newest first, each
with the path of the page that opens it, and the link to compose a new one
(`Next.Systems.Announcement.ComposePage`). Only system admins with the
`announcements` flag on get announcements (`allowed?`).

- [Next.Systems.Announcement.Cards](Next.Systems.Announcement.Cards.md): Announcement cards shared by the Desktop preview and the full list.
- [Next.Systems.Announcement.ComposePage](Next.Systems.Announcement.ComposePage.md): The page to compose an announcement: `/admin/announcement/new` for a new one,
`/admin/announcement/:id` to open one from the list on the Admin page.
Saving stores the announcement unpublished. Publishing sends it to the
audience chosen below the form: creators, narrowed by the Admin → Users
filters and search. The server resolves the audience itself
(`Next.Systems.Announcement.Public.publish_announcement/4`). Saved,
published or cancelled, it goes back to the list.
- [Next.Systems.Announcement.ComposePageBuilder](Next.Systems.Announcement.ComposePageBuilder.md): View model of the page to compose an announcement
(`Next.Systems.Announcement.ComposePage`): the labels of the form and, for an
unpublished one, the audience: who it reaches with the chosen filters and
search, and whether they get an email.
- [Next.Systems.Announcement.DeliverJob](Next.Systems.Announcement.DeliverJob.md): Gives the recipients of a just-published announcement their recipient rows
and To-dos, and for a high-priority announcement their emails
(`Next.Systems.Announcement.Public.deliver_announcement/1`). Running it again
adds and sends nothing, so a retry is safe.

- [Next.Systems.Announcement.DesktopSection](Next.Systems.Announcement.DesktopSection.md): The Announcements section on Desktop, above Recent items: the newest
announcements the user received, read and unread, as cards that each open
the announcement page. Hidden while
the `:announcements` flag is off and for users without announcements.
- [Next.Systems.Announcement.EmailTemplate](Next.Systems.Announcement.EmailTemplate.md): The email of a high-priority announcement, readable on its own: the title,
the full body and a link to the announcement page, without the summary. The
HTML part has the cleaned body; the plain-text part has its text.
- [Next.Systems.Announcement.Model](Next.Systems.Announcement.Model.md): An announcement written by a system admin for a group of creators. The body is
the HTML of the rich-text editor (Trix), stored cleaned
(`Frameworks.Pixel.RichText.clean/1`).
- [Next.Systems.Announcement.NextActions.ReadAnnouncement](Next.Systems.Announcement.NextActions.ReadAnnouncement.md): The To-do of one unread announcement. There is one per recipient, keyed by
the announcement (`key/1`). Title and summary are read from the announcement
when the To-do is shown, so edits show at once. Opening the announcement
page clears it (`Next.Systems.Announcement.Public.mark_read/1`).

- [Next.Systems.Announcement.Page](Next.Systems.Announcement.Page.md): An announcement as its recipient reads it: title, publication date and the
rich-text body. Opening it marks it read and clears its To-do
(`Next.Systems.Announcement.Public.mark_read/1`); Desktop and the To-do counter
refresh through their own switches on `{:next_action, :cleared}`.
- [Next.Systems.Announcement.PageBuilder](Next.Systems.Announcement.PageBuilder.md)
- [Next.Systems.Announcement.Presenter](Next.Systems.Announcement.Presenter.md)
- [Next.Systems.Announcement.Private](Next.Systems.Announcement.Private.md)
- [Next.Systems.Announcement.Public](Next.Systems.Announcement.Public.md): Create, change and read announcements and their recipients.
- [Next.Systems.Announcement.Queries](Next.Systems.Announcement.Queries.md)
- [Next.Systems.Announcement.RecipientModel](Next.Systems.Announcement.RecipientModel.md): One user who received an announcement. `read_at` is set the first time the
user opens it.

- [Next.Systems.Announcement.Routes](Next.Systems.Announcement.Routes.md)
- [Next.Systems.Announcement.Switch](Next.Systems.Announcement.Switch.md): Refreshes the Desktop of every recipient when an announcement changes, so
its Desktop section and To-do show the new title and summary at once, and
the announcement page of a recipient who has it open, so it shows the new
text. Both read the text from the database when the message arrives, so a
message that arrives late never brings back older text.

- [Next.Systems.Announcement.System](Next.Systems.Announcement.System.md): Announcements that system admins write for creators, such as release notes:
the announcement, its rich-text body and the users who received it.

- [Next.Systems.Graphite.LeaderboardModel](Next.Systems.Graphite.LeaderboardModel.md): Data model for the `graphite_leaderboard` table.
# Fields
- title: :string, Title of the leaderboard as will be displayed on the platform
- subtitle: :string, Short subtitle for the leaderboard
- status: :enum (?)
- metrics: {:array, :string}, List of metrics that will be tracked for
  leaderboard.
- visibility: Enum with values
  - public: everybody (including anonymous users) can see team names
  - private: team names are hidden for everybody
- open_date: :naive_datetime, datetime after which everybody can see team names
  for the scores on the leaderboard.
- generation_date: :naive_datetime, the day the scores for the leaderboard were
  generated
- tool_id: connects to `Next.Systems.Graphite.ToolModel`
- auth_node_id: connects to `Mica.Authorization.Node`

- [Systems.Account.AuthCodeCleanupWorker](Systems.Account.AuthCodeCleanupWorker.md): Scheduled Oban worker that prunes auth_codes past their validity window,

- [Systems.Account.AuthCodeLimits](Systems.Account.AuthCodeLimits.md): Limits on sign-in codes on top of the checks each single code allows
(`Systems.Account.AuthCodeModel`). They count per email address, per email
address and network address together, and per network address, in the
database (`Rate.Public.increment_counter/2`), so all nodes share them and
restarts don't reset them. Windows are fixed: a refused address or network
is allowed again when the window ends.

to fund, at what fee, plus the (persisted) study aim.
- [Systems.Fund.PayoutModel](Systems.Fund.PayoutModel.md): Aggregates the `Fund.RewardModel` rows paid out in a single provider withdrawal.
- [Systems.Fund.PayoutOrphanReconciliation](Systems.Fund.PayoutOrphanReconciliation.md): Provider→local reconciliation for payouts: lists the withdrawals and transfers
the provider created inside the window and flags any whose payout has no local
row at all.
- [Systems.Fund.PayoutReconciliation](Systems.Fund.PayoutReconciliation.md): Reconciliation for participant payouts. Dispatches on `PayoutModel.phase/1`:
a payout in flight is driven to its terminal state from the provider's
withdrawal status; a stranded one (funds moved but the withdrawal never
completed) is healed via `Fund.Public.resume_payout/1`; and only a truly
unrecoverable one (an unconfirmed transfer with no findable charge) is flagged
for manual review. Driven by `Systems.Payment.ReconciliationWorker`.

- [Systems.Fund.PayoutWithdrawal](Systems.Fund.PayoutWithdrawal.md): The withdrawal leg of a payout, and its recovery.
- [Systems.Fund.Presenter](Systems.Fund.Presenter.md)
- [Systems.Fund.Public](Systems.Fund.Public.md)
- [Systems.Fund.Queries](Systems.Fund.Queries.md)

- [Systems.Fund.Routes](Systems.Fund.Routes.md)
- [Systems.Fund.System](Systems.Fund.System.md)
- [Systems.Fund.TransactionModel](Systems.Fund.TransactionModel.md)
- [Systems.Fund.TransactionOrphanReconciliation](Systems.Fund.TransactionOrphanReconciliation.md): Provider→local reconciliation for pay-ins: lists the transactions the provider
created inside the window and flags any with no local row.
- [Systems.Fund.TransactionReconciliation](Systems.Fund.TransactionReconciliation.md): Reconciliation for pay-in transactions. Re-applies the provider's current
status to `:pending`/`:failed` transactions whose webhook was lost (including
rescuing one the expiry worker marked `:failed` while the provider actually
completed it), and flags `:completed` transactions the provider has no record
of — a critical discrepancy. Driven by `Systems.Payment.ReconciliationWorker`;
provider calls go through `Systems.Payment.Reconciliation`
(throttle / back-off / circuit breaker) and the shared `ReconciliationState`
is threaded through and returned.

- [Systems.NextAction.ViewModel](Systems.NextAction.ViewModel.md)
- [Systems.Notify.Channel](Systems.Notify.Channel.md): Channel-adapter behaviour. A channel takes a persisted `MessageModel` (with
its event context) and ships it. The dispatcher handles status transitions
based on the return value — adapters just focus on delivery.
- [Systems.Notify.Channel.Email](Systems.Notify.Channel.Email.md): Email channel adapter. Builds a Bamboo email per event and ships it via the
existing `Systems.Email` pipeline.
- [Systems.Notify.Channel.NA](Systems.Notify.Channel.NA.md): Next-Action channel adapter. Creates an NBA on the recipient's Home for the
event, via the existing `Systems.NextAction` infrastructure.
- [Systems.Notify.Dispatcher](Systems.Notify.Dispatcher.md): Event → Messages → Channel delivery.
- [Systems.Notify.EventAttrs](Systems.Notify.EventAttrs.md): Input struct for `Systems.Notify.Public.record_event/1`. Keeps the
contract explicit so callers get a `FunctionClauseError` on the wrong
shape instead of a silent `nil` deep in normalize.

- [Systems.Notify.EventDeclaration](Systems.Notify.EventDeclaration.md): Per-system notification event registration, mirroring the `_routes.ex`
convention. A system opts in by dropping a `_notify.ex`
- [Systems.Notify.EventModel](Systems.Notify.EventModel.md): A raw fact that something happened. Records the "what + who + when" —
channels + timing are decided later by `Systems.Notify.Scheduler`.
- [Systems.Notify.EventType](Systems.Notify.EventType.md): Global registry of notification event types → channel routing.
- [Systems.Notify.MessageModel](Systems.Notify.MessageModel.md): A message produced from an event for one specific channel. Channel adapters
interpret `payload` shape (e.g. email carries `%{subject, text, html}`, NA
carries `%{action_module, key, params}`).

- [Systems.Notify.Public](Systems.Notify.Public.md): Public API for `Systems.Notify`. Domain code calls `record_event/1` from
wherever a notifiable thing happens; the scheduler + channels take it from
there.

- [Systems.Notify.Scheduler](Systems.Notify.Scheduler.md): Decides when + how an event turns into messages.
- [Systems.Notify.System](Systems.Notify.System.md)

- [Systems.Payment.OrphanScan](Systems.Payment.OrphanScan.md): Shared scaffolding for the provider→local passes (`Fund.PayoutOrphanReconciliation`,
`Fund.TransactionOrphanReconciliation`, `Account.MerchantOrphanReconciliation`).
- [Systems.Payment.Plug](Systems.Payment.Plug.md): Caches the raw request body for webhook signature verification.
- [Systems.Payment.Private](Systems.Payment.Private.md)
- [Systems.Payment.Provider](Systems.Payment.Provider.md)
- [Systems.Payment.Provider.Local](Systems.Payment.Provider.Local.md)
- [Systems.Payment.Provider.LocalController](Systems.Payment.Provider.LocalController.md)
- [Systems.Payment.Provider.OPP](Systems.Payment.Provider.OPP.md)
- [Systems.Payment.Provider.OPP.HTTP](Systems.Payment.Provider.OPP.HTTP.md)
- [Systems.Payment.Provider.OPP.Webhook](Systems.Payment.Provider.OPP.Webhook.md)
- [Systems.Payment.Public](Systems.Payment.Public.md)
- [Systems.Payment.Reconciliation](Systems.Payment.Reconciliation.md): Support for the reconciliation sweep: provider calls wrapped with throttling,
back-off and a circuit breaker, plus the run/finding persistence lifecycle.
- [Systems.Payment.ReconciliationFindingModel](Systems.Payment.ReconciliationFindingModel.md): One row per non-trivial reconciliation outcome (anything that was resolved,
could not be resolved, errored, or diverged from the provider). Trivial
outcomes (`:still_pending`, `:verified`) are counted on the run but not stored
here.
- [Systems.Payment.ReconciliationRunModel](Systems.Payment.ReconciliationRunModel.md): One row per reconciliation sweep, recording when it ran and the aggregate
outcome tally. Lets us query reconciliation history without grepping logs.

- [Systems.Payment.ReconciliationState](Systems.Payment.ReconciliationState.md): Accumulator threaded through a reconciliation sweep. Carries the running
`ReconciliationSummary` tally, the list of non-trivial findings to persist,
and the provider circuit-breaker state (consecutive failures → open).

- [Systems.Payment.ReconciliationSummary](Systems.Payment.ReconciliationSummary.md): Tally of a reconciliation run, shared by the per-type reconcilers
(`Fund.Public.reconcile_pending_payouts/1`, `Fund.Public.reconcile_transactions/1`)
and aggregated by `Systems.Payment.ReconciliationWorker`.
- [Systems.Payment.ReconciliationWorker](Systems.Payment.ReconciliationWorker.md): Daily reconciliation sweep. Compares our pay-in (`Budget`) and payout
(`Fund`) state against the payment provider and resolves safe discrepancies — a
lost or failed webhook that left a transaction/payout stuck, or a pay-in the
expiry worker marked `:failed` while the provider actually completed it. It
also flags the critical case the synchronous path can't: local terminal state
the provider has no record of.

* <platform>.svg (circle variant)
* <platform>_square.svg (square variant)

## Mix Tasks

- [mix config.snapshot](Mix.Tasks.Config.Snapshot.md): Evaluates `config/runtime.exs` with the environment variables of each
deployment (fixtures in `next/test/config/env/`) and compares the result
with the committed snapshots in `next/test/config/snapshots/`.
- [mix e2e](Mix.Tasks.E2e.md): Run Playwright E2E tests in `core/test/e2e/` against any environment.
- [mix next.graphite.del.submissions](Mix.Tasks.Next.Graphite.Del.Submissions.md): Remove Submissions generated with the generate submissions command.
- [mix next.graphite.gen.submissions](Mix.Tasks.Next.Graphite.Gen.Submissions.md): Generate a number of submissions for a `leaderboard`.
- [mix nova.snapshot](Mix.Tasks.Nova.Snapshot.md): Captures what a SaaS build wires together, so that the Nova migration
(plan step code-systems) can move routes, grants, handlers and SaaS config
between modules and show that nothing changed. The snapshots per SaaS are
committed in `next/test/snapshots/<saas>/`
- [mix seed](Mix.Tasks.Seed.md): Runs `Mica.Seeds.seed/0` which executes base seeds plus
environment-specific seeds based on the `:deploy_env` config.
- [mix storybook.gen](Mix.Tasks.Storybook.Gen.md): Writes a `*.story.exs` for every public function component (`def` with `attr`/`slot`
declarations) defined under SOURCE_DIR that has no story in CONTENT_DIR yet. Existing stories are
never touched, so curate a story by editing its generated file.
